title: Prompt and Response Flow
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Artificial Intelligence
Large Language Models
Prompt Engineering
System Prompt
Nondeterminism
description: Clickable left-to-right flowchart showing how a system prompt and a user prompt are tokenized and combined in a single model request, how the language model samples a response, and why the same inputs can produce a different response on the next run. Clicking a node shows its definition in a shared infobox.

educational.topic: System prompts, user prompts, and nondeterministic model output
learningObjectives: Differentiate the role of a system prompt from a user prompt in a single model request.
Explain why the same inputs can produce a different response on the next run.
prerequisites: Knows what a token is and what tokenization does
Has read the definitions of prompt and system prompt

controls.label: Flowchart node
controls.description: Each of the six nodes has a Mermaid click directive that shows its definition and role in the shared infobox below the diagram

controls.label: Tab and Enter
controls.description: Nodes can be focused with Tab and selected with Enter or Space

pedagogical.pattern: Clickable flow diagram with comparison table
pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Click-to-reveal definitions plus a side-by-side comparison of the two prompt types
keyQuestions: What does the system prompt contribute that the user prompt does not?
Why can two runs with identical prompts return different responses?
commonMisconceptions: A model computes one fixed answer for a given prompt
The system prompt and the user prompt are the same thing typed in different places
assessmentOpportunities: Sort a list of instructions into system prompt or user prompt and justify each choice
